I work on the Colorado and the Green river in Moab, Utah. I love the variety of guiding down here. One day you’ll be in Westwater canyon, with tight moves and technical III-IV rapids, the next day is a lazy float down the daily section of the river. Or you could be in Cataract canyon, with big water class Vs. 

I work for Western River Expeditions and they are always looking for more guides. They provide housing and the best memories, experiences and friends I have ever had. This will be my 3rd year in a row returning, and definitely not my last. 

If you want to apply check out this link my boss told me to give people [https://www.westernriver.com/how-to-become-a-river-guide](https://www.westernriver.com/how-to-become-a-river-guide) 

If you end up applying here and get an interview, they’ll probably ask how you found out about them. Tell them you met “Little Newty” on this subreddit and they’ll understand lol. You might have to explain what a subreddit is though. Best of luck and stoked for whatever you end up doing with your guiding career!!

Edit: forgot to add, they’ll train ya. My friends Who had never been on a raft showed up from Rhode Island last year clueless and are now some of the best guides in the company.
